chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “No forty nights pass over the believer except that a matter occurs to him which grieves him, by which he is reminded.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ: forty; indicating a limited span after which a trial or reminder occurs
key_terms.أَمْرٌ: a matter or event that befalls a person
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer; the person characterized by true faith
key_terms.لَيْلَةً: nights; the period mentioned in the narration
key_terms.يُذَكَّرُ بِهِ: by which he is reminded or admonished

ai.seo_question: Why do hardships and grief regularly come to a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a believer is not left for long without an occurrence that brings grief and serves as a reminder. It highlights the spiritual role of affliction in keeping the believer mindful and spiritually awakened.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Momin, forty days would not pass over him except a matter would present itself to him, grieving him, preoccupying him with it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim
from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Before forty days pass something causes sadness to a believer to remind him.”
